description: REQ-002's edge case explicitly requires: 'citizens.json missing/unreadable/malformed JSON: refuse.' The production read_citizens() implementation has no try/except around open()/json.load(), and run_refill() calls deps['read_citizens']() at line 150 with no surrounding try/except either -- unlike every other identity-resolution step in the same function (derive_pubkey IS wrapped in try/except at lines 143-148). A missing, unreadable, or malformed ~/.hermes/state/citizens.json therefore raises an UNCAUGHT exception that crashes the whole process instead of the clean fail-closed refusal (JSON stdout line + ledger row) every other refusal path produces. This also breaks the module's own documented output contract ('exactly one JSON line on stdout... non-zero otherwise' -- franklin_sol_base_refill.py:28-29): a crash emits a Python traceback, not a JSON line, and appends NO ledger row recording the refusal (every other refusal path calls fail(), which appends a row). No orchestration test ever makes read_citizens() raise or return malformed data -- the injected fixture in tests/test_franklin_sol_base_refill.py's make_deps() always returns a valid [FRANKLIN_ROW] list, so this explicit, named spec edge case is both unimplemented (as fail-closed-with-ledger-row) and untested.
